body:
**Stable key:** `MEM-P09`  
**Difficulty:** **High**  
**Suggested label:** `difficulty:high` (metadata proposal; a title/body marker does not depend on label availability)  
**Planning baseline:** `Ozwasyd/FsusBlog@580cf1af614fd0edab9cb4c9ee95ec4e128b0327`  
**Acceptance predecessors:** `MEM-P01` (#3445), `MEM-P08` (#3450)

### Objective

Make budgets adapt automatically to valid pressure observations and actual reclamation while retaining hard boundaries and correctness.

### Source and scope precedence

This issue implements stage P09 of the user-supplied memory-governance report (version 1.0, 2026-09-15). The user's later requirement for default automatic discovery and activation supersedes `Preferred`, default-off, and mandatory manual-per-capability opt-in wording. Original work-item IDs are preserved for traceability. Baseline paths must be checked against the actual implementation candidate; this issue is not a claim that proposed types already exist.

### Mandatory policy and terminology

All configurable capabilities default to `Auto` when omitted. `Auto` means automatic discovery, bounded qualification, online activation, and deterministic selection for an eligible workload after resource admission. It does not mean indiscriminate allocation. A supported, release-qualified and runtime-qualified available path must not require a second enable flag, per-host approval file, or administrator confirmation. `Disabled` prevents new capability-specific probes and use, and drains existing owners before disposal. `Required` adds a strict requirement; it does not override safety, permissions, qualification, or budgets. The earlier report value `Preferred` is superseded, not an additional mode.

Detection, qualification, online state, effective path, and per-operation admission are separate facts. Unknown, Unsupported, NotVerified, Faulted, Disabled, and temporarily BudgetRejected are not synonyms. A missing signal is not zero usage. Qualifying a release/backend is not a manual opt-in on each deployment. The always-required accounting, ownership, and content-security rules are not optional capability switches.

### Scope and exclusions

No always-200 promise, arbitrary fixed percentage thresholds, forced release of active readers, whole-cache VRAM evacuation, or global OS-policy change is included.

All product implementation introduced by this memory program remains C#/.NET. Supported already-installed OS/GPU APIs may be called through isolated C# adapters. Existing unrelated C++, frontend, protocol, and business components are not rewritten. Do not change AEDS/HTTP, authorization, revocation, publication, or delivery authority merely to simplify memory management.

### Files and ownership

| Status | Path or owner | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Control/` | MemoryGovernor, immutable decisions, pure transition function, and reclaim feedback. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Accounting/` | Enforce both owned capacity and scoped external-pressure gates. |
| R | `Existing admission, refresh, and quota adapters` | Keep established work owners and attach decision inputs. |
| N | `Governor replay and resource-domain tests under current test ownership` | Use the P01 numerical acceptance manifest. |

B = baseline-reported; N = proposed-new; R = exact owner unresolved until MEM-P00. Paths and namespaces in this table are scope locators, not permission to create a parallel registry, publisher, scheduler, configuration source, or test runner. New tests must reside inside the actual owning project.

### Required implementation work

- [ ] **P09.1** Publish immutable, revisioned control outputs for resident targets, build/materialization/migration/I/O slots, transient budgets, promotion permission, reclamation requests, and bounded reason codes. Consumers read decisions at operation boundaries, not through a new L0 control round trip.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P09-AC01`, `MEM-P09-AC10`.
- [ ] **P09.2** Implement a deterministic decision function over validated samples, ledger, effective external/configured constraints, and previous state. Apply both the application ownership hard gate and scoped external-pressure gates. Report Infeasible when protected and in-flight commitments cannot fit.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P09-AC02`, `MEM-P09-AC03`, `MEM-P09-AC07`.
- [ ] **P09.3** Implement asymmetric response, entry/exit hysteresis, minimum stable recovery windows, and bounded growth. A lower target stops incompatible new work but does not revoke valid leases or submitted operations.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P09-AC03`, `MEM-P09-AC04`.
- [ ] **P09.4** Use sustained swap activity, pressure/stall observations, and measured service degradation as feedback. Freeze promotion and reduce costly work when qualified signals require it; do not clear a healthy hot set because historical swap occupancy is nonzero.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P09-AC06`.
- [ ] **P09.5** Apply an explicit degradation order: stop speculative work and refills, reclaim unheld reconstructible or already-backed cold copies, reduce optional residency, admit only bounded spill, and reduce expensive work. Preserve content qualification and original error/withdrawal behavior.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P09-AC05`, `MEM-P09-AC07`.
- [ ] **P09.6** Consume actual requested/reclaimed/pending/blocked feedback. Distinguish logical target changes, allocator relinquishment, OS retention, slow readers, writeback, and infeasible protection. A governor fault freezes growth and preserves hard gates instead of disabling enforcement.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P09-AC05`, `MEM-P09-AC08`, `MEM-P09-AC09`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC01** The same sample sequence, ledger state, policy revision, and test clock produce the same ordered decisions. Each decision includes sequence, source ages, reason, and effective constraints.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC02** The ownership hard gate cannot be passed by a low RSS measurement for allocated-but-untouched memory. Overlapping GC, process, native, pinned, and UMA observations are not summed as independent usage or capacity.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC03** T04/T23 reduce a target or external bound below commitments. The next decision within the configured reaction window blocks incompatible new work, retains the old charges, and exposes over-target or Infeasible state.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC04** T27 proves distinct entry/exit rules, the declared stable recovery window, and the maximum growth rate. Oscillating input does not cause alternating uncontrolled promotion and eviction.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC05** T28 distinguishes requested, allocator-reclaimed, pending, and blocked bytes. Shrinking a target to zero cannot report successful reclamation while a reader, operation, shared block, or retained pool still owns the bytes.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC06** T24 and T26 do not mechanically force a swap emergency. T25 triggers its predeclared response, and measured latency/reclamation outcomes or nonrecovery causes are recorded without claiming correlation alone proves causation.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC07** No degraded state bypasses authorization, revocation, representation identity, hard admission, or existing queue-delivery semantics. No valid stale result results in the existing failure/retry behavior, not an unconditional HTTP 200.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC08** T54 injects an exception and prolonged missing observations. Expansion stops, existing operations drain safely, and current hard constraints remain enforced with bounded diagnostics.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC09** Adaptive governance participates in the default Auto policy. Restoring qualified observations and the configured stable window automatically permits safe recovery; no operator action is required to re-enable normal growth.
- [ ] **MEM-P09-AC10** Governor ticks and reclaim scheduling stay within their configured CPU, allocation, queue-count, and queue-byte limits. They do not perform device initialization or synchronous I/O on an L0 hit.

### Required validation scope

Deterministic governor replay and real source/control integration. Unimplemented disk/device executors may be modeled for decision tests, but complete spill/device behavior remains required by their owners.

| Scenario | Responsibility in this issue | Required observable assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `T01`: Concurrent requests for the final host budget | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P03 | Accepted unique charges plus unconsumed reservations never exceed the configured hard gate; failed requests leave no partial grant. |
| `T04`: Budget revision drops below live reservations | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P03 | Live charge remains visible, incompatible growth stops, and over-target/Infeasible is reported without fabricated release. |
| `T21`: Missing, denied, malformed, or stale pressure source | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P08 | Retain Unknown and provenance; do not authorize growth from stale or fabricated zero values. |
| `T23`: External limit reduction or process resource-domain migration | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P08 | Invalidate old identity/observations and tighten new admission within the declared reaction bound. |
| `T24`: Nonzero swap occupancy without sustained swap activity | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P08 | Do not classify healthy residency as thrashing or mechanically empty the hot set. |
| `T25`: Sustained swap I/O, stalls, and tail-latency degradation | Primary implementation owner | Apply the predeclared control response and measure actual reclaim and service outcomes or explain nonrecovery. |
| `T26`: File major faults rise without anonymous-swap evidence | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P08 | Do not attribute all faults to swap; preserve source classification and uncertainty. |
| `T27`: Oscillating pressure near thresholds and later recovery | Primary implementation owner | Enforce entry/exit hysteresis, the minimum stable window, and bounded growth. |
| `T28`: Target shrinks while readers or allocators retain capacity | Primary implementation owner | Separate requested from actual reclamation; report blocked ownership rather than a false recovery. |
| `T29`: Growing pressure with no swap | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P12 | Prepare replicas while reaction headroom exists; avoid large new copy/write storms in Critical. |
| `T53`: Continuous pressure events and diagnostics | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P20 | Bound buffers, log volume, and label cardinality and prevent private-data disclosure. |
| `T54`: Controller fault or prolonged observation failure | Primary implementation owner | Freeze growth and retain conservative hard admission with truthful degraded diagnostics. |

### Evidence and acceptance rules

Every unchecked acceptance criterion below is mandatory. `must` and `must not` are normative; `may` grants an option only where it is explicitly stated. A required test passes only when its specified assertion is observed on the current candidate. A comment stating that an assertion is true is not evidence.

Bind evidence to the actual commit and worktree fingerprint, fixture, toolchain, configuration revision, backend, OS/architecture, relevant driver/device identity, actual command, and raw result. Use the existing test DAG, required static admission, fixture ownership, and independent verifiers. All numeric limits and performance expressions referenced by this issue must be finite, explicit, and frozen by their owning policy/baseline before candidate results are examined. Missing values block acceptance; do not invent a passing threshold afterward.

Expected resource rejection must not conceal use-after-free, bounds violations, double free, uninitialized disclosure, revoked/wrong content, negative accounting, a parallel authority, or an unbounded queue. Any such correctness failure blocks acceptance regardless of performance. Do not rewrite frozen receipts or weaken tests. Missing platform or hardware evidence is `NotVerified`, not `Passed` or a convenient `NotApplicable`.

Evidence level is stage-specific: contract or fixture work may run before a downstream backend exists, but it does not certify that backend. Each primary implementation owner must supply its own required integration/platform evidence; MEM-P19 independently closes the complete matrix. Passing tests never authorizes automatic closure of this issue, another issue, or a pull request.

### Safe disable and rollback

Use an explicitly selected conservative static target without discarding live reservations or the latest valid external hard bound. Fault handling must never fall back to unlimited allocation.

### Completion report

Report the exact scope and files changed, every acceptance-criterion result, tests and commands actually run, raw current-source evidence, default Auto behavior, negative/competition cases, performance against frozen gates where applicable, unresolved support rows, and rollback results. A missing required environment leaves the corresponding promise unverified. Do not describe planned tests or a passing document validator as product verification.

Docker-related tests are not to be executed by this delivery agent under the project restriction. State them explicitly as not run. A Docker-specific assertion requires evidence from its authorized owner; a genuinely technology-independent assertion may use authorized non-Docker isolation. Do not fetch missing implementation dependencies from the network; record exact package/version/target gaps and stop the blocked execution item.
